articles.title_original: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
articles.title_zh: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
facts_zh:
Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
- Published
Five people have been killed and 16 injured in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say.
Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.
The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said they struck "the Saudi enemy's military operations headquarters in Aden".

all_titles.en: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says

articles.title_original: Tip-off foiled US teen suspect's plot to attack Hindu temple, police say
articles.title_zh: Tip-off foiled US teen suspect's plot to attack Hindu temple, police say
facts_zh:
Tip-off foiled US teen's plot to attack Hindu temple, police say
- Published
A Taco Bell cashier's alleged plot for a mass shooting at a Hindu temple near Chicago was thwarted by a tip-off from one of his colleagues, investigators say.
Alexandros Paporakis, 19, from Palatine, Illinois, appeared in court on Wednesday charged with one count of making a terrorist threat and one count of unlawful possession of a weapon.
Paporakis allegedly sent a message about the planned attack on Sunday to the co-worker, who alerted authorities, officials said.

articles.title_zh: Letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to US senators and election offices
facts_zh:
Letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to US senators and election offices
- Published
Federal authorities say they are investigating "potentially hazardous" letters containing "suspicious substances" that have been sent to congressional and state election offices around the US.
The FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) said they were trying to trace the "suspicious mailings", some of which were intercepted before they were received.
Authorities declined to say how many offices had been targeted, but several secretaries of state and congressional offices reported receiving the letters.

all_titles.en: Letters with 'suspicious substances' sent to US senators and election offices

articles.title_original: Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
articles.title_zh: Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
facts_zh:
Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
- Published
A bus has hit a stationary freight train near the French entrance to the Channel Tunnel, injuring the driver and 18 passengers, French authorities say.
The bus, which was carrying lorry drivers due to take a shuttle rail service, struck the train at the loading platform of the tunnel in Coquelles, near Calais, at 19:27 (18:27 BST) on Thursday.
The bus driver and one passenger were severely injured and evacuated by helicopter.

facts_zh:
Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad
- Published
US President Donald Trump has called off plans to livestream the execution of former US army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan by firing squad.
Trump had previously said he approved of showing the death of the Fort Hood attacker, while Vice-President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would happen and said he would not watch it.
Trump's decision to cancel the livestream came after widespread criticism in the US and globally.

articles.title_zh: Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
facts_zh:
Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
- Published
Venezuela's former leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, appeared in court on Thursday to plead not guilty to new charges of conspiracy to commit torture.
The US government initially accused Maduro of narco-terrorism, drug trafficking and weapons-related offenses, before adding new charges against him and Flores last week.
Maduro and Flores were captured in January during a US military raid, after which they were taken to New York, where they remain in jail.

articles.title_original: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
articles.title_zh: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
facts_zh:
School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
- Published
"You are telling me, I can't come to school?" says a teenage girl in a navy blue Islamic headscarf, captured on video challenging a staff member at the entrance to her school.

The footage has been shared widely on social media, and shows a group of girls in hijabs standing behind her applauding as she continues: "Why should I have to give up my religion?"
Last Monday the education ministry in Azerbaijan began enforcing new uniform rules, turning away female pupils wearing hijabs.
Protests began outside state schools in the capital, Baku, and in several southern districts including Masally and Jalilabad.

all_titles.en: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey

articles.title_zh: Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
facts_zh:
Seven crew missing after drone attack leaves tanker ablaze off Romania's coast
- Published
Seven of 12 crew members are missing after a drone attack left a chemical tanker ablaze off Romania's coast on Thursday morning, naval authorities say.
The San Marino-flagged Wine Trader was 13 nautical miles (24km) east of the mouth of the River Danube at Sulina, when it reported blasts and a fire.
Romanian President Nicușor Dan confirmed that the Wine Trader and another chemical tanker in the area, the Yara J, had both been struck by drones - the Yara J on Wednesday.
